text: Even today my complaint is bitter; his hand lies heavy in spite of my groaning.

versions.text: Even today my complaint is bitter; his hand is heavy on me despite my groaning.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has no "on me" (the phrase is literally "the hand is heavy upon my groaning"), and the Masoretic text actually reads "my hand," with "his hand" resting on ancient versional evidence. Removing the added "on me" keeps the line tighter for reading aloud; a footnote such as "Or 'my hand is heavy because of my groaning'" would help the reader.

text: If only I knew where to find him, if only I could come to his dwelling!
I would lay my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
I would learn what he would answer me and understand what he would say.
Would he contend against me with his great power? No, he would surely listen to me.

versions.text: Would he overpower me with his great strength? No, he would surely give me a hearing.
versions.explanation: The verb יָרִיב is a legal term meaning "contend, bring suit," continuing the courtroom imagery of verses 4-7; "overpower" loses that legal sense. "Listen to me" also renders יָשִׂם בִּי ("pay attention to me") more naturally for oral reading than the formal idiom "give me a hearing."

text: There an upright man could reason with him, and I would be acquitted forever by my judge.
But if I go east, he is not there; if west, I cannot perceive him.
When he is at work in the north, I cannot see him; when he turns to the south, I catch no glimpse of him.
Yet he knows the way I take; when he has tested me, I will come out as gold.
My feet have held fast to his steps; I have kept to his way and not turned aside.
I have not departed from the command of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my own desire.

versions.text: I have not departed from the command of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my daily bread.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מֵחֻקִּי means "than my own decree/portion"; rendering it "my daily bread" imports a specific interpretive choice that may puzzle hearers. If "daily bread" is retained, a footnote is advisable: "Hebrew 'more than my own portion'; the sense may be 'in my heart I have stored up his words.'"

text: But he stands alone, and who can turn him back? What he desires, that he does.
He will carry out what he has decreed for me, and many such plans are still with him.
That is why I am terrified before him; when I consider it, I am afraid of him.
God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has filled me with terror.
Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick gloom that covers my face.
